atoms.text: Marie Curie was a very important scientist whose contributions we still benefit from today. She was born in Poland on November 7, 1867. Marie Curie was the first woman to win the Nobel Prize and the first person to ever win the prize twice.
atoms.sound: Marry Curie was a very important scientist whose contributions we still benefit from today. She was born in Poland on November 7, 1867. Marry Curie was the first woman to win the Nobel Prize and the first person to ever win the prize twice.

atoms.text: The majority of her research was in the field of radiation and examined substances and minerals for signs of radioactivity. Marie Curie discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium. Her discoveries led to further important scientific research.
atoms.sound: The majority of her research was in the field of radiation and examined substances and minerals for signs of radioactivity. Marry Curie discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium. Her discoveries led to further important scientific research.

atoms.text: Understanding radiation is incredibly important because it can be used for scientific experiments and in medicine to see inside someone’s body and look for tumours or broken bones. Unfortunately, Marie Curie died in 1934 in Paris due to her lengthy exposure to radioactive elements. Radiation in large doses is deadly, as radioactivity can destroy cells in the body.
